newsitem.title: INDIA: India keeps MAT tax but exempts export profits.
newsitem.headline: India keeps MAT tax but exempts export profits.

text.p: India on Friday proposed keeping a minimum alternate tax (MAT) on company profits which was introduced in the last budget, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said while presenting the 1997/98 (April-March) budget.
"The economic rationale for MAT has, I'm afraid, not been altered, and I am unable to accept the request that the provision introduced last year be totally withdrawn," Chidambaram told parliament.
But he proposed diluting the tax by exempting export profits from MAT.
Chidambaram said he would introduce a "system of credit" for the payment of MAT.
MAT -- a 12.9 percent tax on company profits -- was introduced in the 1996/97 budget last July to bring some of India's top companies in the tax dragnet.
"When a company pays MAT, the tax credit earned by it shall be allowed to be carried forward for a period of five assesment years," the finance minister said.
He said in the assessment year when regular tax becomes payable the difference between regular tax and tax computed under MAT would be set off against the MAT credit available.
